research_rationale: I read the complete held Federal Register original of Executive Order 7577 (2 FR 671, March 24, 1937; signed March 19, 1937). It is one order that amends section XV-4 of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers and section 451 of the Consular Regulations to read as a new text on presents and testimonials, and that text prohibits diplomatic and consular officers from accepting any present, decoration, medal, order or testimonial from a foreign king, prince or state. It has no duration, condition, report or savings language. I read the complete held Federal Register text of Executive Order 8396 (5 FR 1461, April 20, 1940; signed April 18, 1940). Under its heading revoking executive orders, it states that the listed executive orders are revoked, and the list includes Executive Order No. 7577 dated March 19, 1937, with no condition, exception or deferred effective date. That express revocation is the first end of the order. I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them: the U.S. Code search (edition through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted in the last five days before the 2026-10-14 cutoff are not reflected) and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) found no citation of this order, and the Federal Register disposition-note search found the revocation by Executive Order 8396 and a catalog note that is blank about its effect, which the held revocation text supplies. No held instrument restores or revives Executive Order 7577 after the revocation. Original not an original grade issue: the Federal Register text layer is machine extracted and was checked only as text; the page images were not inspected.
savings_reason: Executive Order 8396 revokes Executive Order 7577 with no saving clause, exception or description of any accrued right or pending matter. The constitutional and statutory provisions that the amended text itself cites continue on their own authority and are not residual commands of Executive Order 7577. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Federal Register disposition notes located no surviving command of this order.
earlier_end_check: The order has no end date, condition, report deadline or sunset in its own words; the three machine own-terms hits are sentences inside the quoted regulation text about gifts from foreign governments, not duration terms. The only held later instrument that names this order is Executive Order 8396, which revokes it; the status-history catalog lists only that revocation, and its note on the order is blank about effect, so the revocation text itself is the basis. A search of the held order-text folders by number, with OCR-tolerant patterns, found no earlier instrument that names, amends or suspends Executive Order 7577. The amending command was performed when the order was issued; the revocation ends the order itself, and no held source shows an earlier ending.
scope_check: The revocation names Executive Order 7577 as a whole, with no partial limiter, no deferred effective date and no exception. The order has one operative clause (the amending command and the text it prescribes), and the inventory covers it from the heading to the end of the prescribed text; the machine note that segmentation is only a lead was resolved by reading the whole order. The end date is the signing date of Executive Order 8396, April 18, 1940, because the revoking order has no effective-date wording; it was filed April 19 and published April 20, 1940, which are later dates and are not used. If revocation were read as effective on filing or publication, the end would move by one or two days.
independent_command_check: The only command is the amendment of the two regulation texts, which took effect when the order was issued. The order contains no report, delegation, appropriation or standing authority apart from that text. The prohibition in the prescribed text rests on the Constitution (Article I, section 9, clause 8) and on statutes that the text cites; those sources are independent of Executive Order 7577 and are not its commands. After the express revocation no command of Executive Order 7577 remains.
savings_check: Executive Order 8396 contains no saving or exception clause for Executive Order 7577. The constitutional and statutory sources cited inside the amended text continue on their own authority and are not residuals of this order. No held source describes a right, appointment or proceeding that survived the revocation.

research_rationale: I read the complete held Federal Register original of Executive Order 8168 (4 FR 2415, June 16, 1939; signed June 14, 1939). It has no duration, condition or savings language. I read the complete held Federal Register text of Executive Order 8854 (6 FR 4181, August 20, 1941; signed August 16, 1941), titled as revoking Executive Order 8168. The Federal Register text layer renders the order number in the quotation as 81681 (a footnote mark run into the number); the actual checker reads that as a different order and reports a mechanical order-exists failure, which is an extraction artifact. An American Presidency Project transcription of the same order is held and agrees in substance, but an official copy is held, so the transcription may not be used as the quoted source. Paragraph 1 orders that Executive Order No. 8168 of June 14, 1939, is revoked, with no condition or exception. Paragraph 2 separately withdraws the lands contained in the 8168 reservation and an adjoining tract for the same Survey use under the President's own authority. Paragraph 2 is a new reservation made by Executive Order 8854, not a continuation of Executive Order 8168, so the whole of Executive Order 8168 ended on August 16, 1941. I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them: the U.S. Code search (through 2026-10-09) and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) found no citation of this order, and the Federal Register disposition-note search found only the revocation by Executive Order 8854 (two catalog entries for the same event).
